item.title: Learn from Japan in the Era of Space Management (우주경영 시대, 일본에서 배워라)
item.description:
Learn from Japan in the Era of Space Management (우주경영 시대, 일본에서 배워라)

Recently, the government has been successively unveiling blueprints to foster space as a future growth engine. Oh Tae-seok, head of the Korea AeroSpace Administration, announced earlier this month in the 'Space and Aerospace Industry Promotion Strategy' that they will secure communication sovereignty by building a Korean low-orbit satellite communication network (K-Starlink) utilizing hundreds of satellites by 2035. The timeline for a lunar landing has also been moved up from the existing 2032 to 2030, with a goal to expand the global space market share from the current 0.7% to 3% (approximately 70 trillion won). (최근 정부가 우주를 미래 성장 동력으로 육성하겠다는 청사진을 잇달아 내놓고 있습니다. 오태석 우주항공청장은 이달 초 ‘우주항공산업 육성 전략’을 발표하며 2035년까지 수백 기의 위성을 활용한 한국형 저궤도 위성 통신망(K-Starlink)을 구축해 통신 주권을 확보하겠다고 밝혔습니다. 달 착륙 시점도 기존 2032년에서 2030년으로 앞당기고, 세계 우주 시장 점유율을 현재 0.7%에서 3%(약 70조원 규모)까지 확대하겠다는 목표도 제시했습니다.)

The direction of making space a new growth engine for the Republic of Korea is commendable. While participating in the previous administration's Future Space Economy Roadmap Task Force under the National Science and Technology Advisory Council, I watched the government's growing interest in the space economy with delight. At the same time, I have come to believe that we need to more actively benchmark Japan, which is utilizing space as a national strategy far ahead of us. (우주를 대한민국의 새로운 성장 동력으로 삼겠다는 방향은 바람직한 일입니다. 저는 전 정부의 국가과학기술자문회의 미래 우주 경제 로드맵 TF에 참여하면서 정부가 우주 경제에 관심을 기울이는 모습을 반갑게 지켜봤습니다. 그러면서 우리보다 훨씬 앞서 우주를 국가 전략으로 활용하고 있는 일본을 더욱 적극적으로 벤치마킹해야 한다는 생각을 해왔습니다.)

The Expanding U.S.-Japan Alliance into Space (우주로 팽창하는 미일동맹)

The most noteworthy aspect of Japan's space strategy is, I believe, the 'U.S.-Japan Space Alliance' that Japan is building with all its might. Even a little over a decade ago, space cooperation between Japan and the U.S. was primarily centered on science and technology and was not particularly prominent. However, it has now developed into a de facto space security alliance encompassing missile defense, military satellites, space surveillance, and lunar exploration. The atmosphere is one of rapid expansion beyond land, sea, and air into space. (일본의 우주 전략에서 가장 주목할 점은 일본이 전력을 다해 구축 중인 ‘미일 우주 동맹’이 아닐까 생각합니다. 불과 10여 년 전까지만 해도 일본과 미국의 우주 협력은 과학기술 중심으로 크게 두드러지지 않았습니다. 그러나 지금은 미사일 방어, 군사 위성, 우주 감시, 달 탐사까지 포함하는 사실상의 우주 안보 동맹으로 발전하고 있습니다. 지상과 해상, 공중을 넘어 우주로 빠르게 확장되는 분위기입니다.)

A recent representative example is Japan's decision to participate in the U.S.'s next-generation missile defense system, the 'Golden Dome.' Reuters reported in March that Japan had agreed to join the Golden Dome construction project and was consulting on related cooperation measures. Japan, with its satellite sensor and precision manufacturing technology, is being evaluated as a key partner in this project, which uses hundreds to thousands of low-earth orbit satellites to detect and track ballistic missiles and hypersonic missiles. (최근 대표적인 사례가 미국의 차세대 미사일 방어 체계인 ‘골든 돔(Golden Dome)’에 일본이 참여하기로 한 것입니다. 로이터통신은 지난 3월 골든 돔 구축 사업에 일본이 참여하기로 하고 관련 협력 방안을 협의 중이라고 보도한 바 있습니다. 수백~수천 기의 저궤도 위성을 활용해 탄도미사일과 극초음속 미사일을 탐지·추적하는 이 사업에 위성 센서와 정밀 제조 기술을 갖춘 일본은 핵심 파트너로 평가받고 있습니다.)

Military space cooperation between the two countries has also reached a high level. Last year, the U.S. Space Force installed a Space Domain Awareness sensor on Japan's Quasi-Zenith Satellite QZS-6. This is the first instance of placing a U.S. military sensor on a Japanese satellite, serving to monitor the movements of Chinese and Russian satellites. The U.S. Space Force highly praised it as the "first bilateral national security space cooperation project between the U.S. and Japan." (양국의 우주 군사 협력도 높은 수준에 이르고 있습니다. 미국 우주군은 지난해 일본의 준천정위성(準天頂衛星) QZS-6에 우주 영역 인식(Space Domain Awareness) 센서를 탑재했습니다. 일본 위성에 미국 군사 센서를 실은 첫 사례로, 중국과 러시아 위성의 움직임을 감시하는 역할을 수행합니다. 미국 우주군은 “미일 최초의 양자 국가안보 우주협력 사업”이라고 높이 평가했습니다.)

Lunar Exploration Also Pursued Jointly (달 탐사도 함께 추진)

Japan is also the most important partner for the U.S. in the newly promoted lunar exploration efforts. Following the establishment of its space force unit in 2020, Japan has participated as a key partner in the U.S. Artemis project. Artemis, from Greek mythology, refers to the twin sister of the sun god Apollo and the goddess of the moon. This plan proceeds in three stages: unmanned lunar orbital flight → manned lunar orbital flight → launch of a lunar landing spacecraft. The focus is on exploration activities to find resources scarce on Earth, including water. (미국이 새롭게 추진중인 달 탐사에서도 일본은 미국의 가장 중요한 파트너입니다. 일본은 2020년 우주부대를 창설한 데 이어 미국의 아르테미스(Artemis) 프로젝트에 핵심 파트너로 참여했습니다. 아르테미스는 그리스 신화에 나오는 태양의 신 아폴론의 쌍둥이 남매로 달의 여신을 의미합니다. 이 계획은 달 궤도 무인 비행→ 달 궤도 유인 비행→ 달 착륙 우주선 발사 등 3단계로 진행됩니다. 이를 통해 물을 비롯, 지구에서 부족한 자원을 찾는 탐사활동에 주력한다는 겁니다.)

In particular, the U.S. and Japan are paying attention to a substance called Helium-3 on the lunar surface. It is known that 1 gram of Helium-3 can produce energy equivalent to 40 tons of coal. Some studies suggest the moon has enough Helium-3 to supply Earth for several hundred years. Artemis also includes plans to mine rare earth elements used in advanced industries and bring them back to Earth. In the long term, it is a mega-project involving installing the 'Gateway' space station in lunar orbit and embarking on Mars exploration. (특히 미국과 일본은 달 표면의 헬륨3라는 물질에 주목하고 있습니다. 헬륨3 1g은 석탄 40t에 해당하는 에너지를 만들어낼 수 있는 것으로 알려졌습니다. 달에는 지구가 수백 년 사용할 수 있는 헬륨3가 있다는 연구도 있습니다. 아르테미스에는 첨단 산업에 쓰이는 희토류를 채굴해 지구로 가져오는 구상도 있습니다. 장기적으로는 달 궤도에 우주정거장 ‘게이트웨이’를 설치하고 화성 탐사에 나서는 초대형 프로젝트입니다.)

NASA signed a lunar exploration cooperation agreement with Japan, agreeing to deploy Japan's developed manned lunar rover into this program. In return, Japan secured opportunities for Japanese astronauts to land on the moon. Japan is effectively the first country other than the U.S. to be formally guaranteed a lunar landing opportunity by the U.S. (NASA는 일본과 달 탐사 협력 협정을 체결, 일본이 개발하는 유인 달 탐사차를 이 프로그램에 투입하기로 했습니다. 일본은 그 대가로 일본인 우주 비행사의 달 착륙 기회를 제공받기로 했습니다. 미국이 자국 이외 국가에 달 착륙 기회를 공식 보장한 것은 사실상 일본이 처음입니다.)

Japan and the U.S., A New Perception of Space (일본과 미국, 우주를 새롭게 인식)

Behind this cooperation lies a shift in strategy by both the U.S. and Japan. U.S. President Trump, from his first term, defined space as a new warfighting domain, following land, sea, air, and cyberspace. Accordingly, the Space Policy Directive-4 was issued in 2019, and the U.S. Space Force was established as an independent military service branch the same year. The Space Force was launched as the sixth branch, following the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard. (이 같은 협력의 배경에는 미국과 일본의 전략 변화가 있습니다. 트럼프 미국 대통령은 1기 임기 때부터 우주를 육·해·공·사이버에 이은 새로운 전장(warfighting domain)으로 규정했습니다. 이에 따라 2019년 우주정책지침(Space Policy Directive-4)을 발표하고 같은 해 미국 ‘우주군(U.S. Space Force)’을 독립 군종으로 창설했습니다. 우주군이 육군·해군·공군·해병대·해안경비대에 이은 여섯 번째 군종으로 출범한 겁니다.)

After the Liberal Democratic Party returned to power in 2012, Japan has consistently pursued the concept of expanding the Self-Defense Forces' operational scope into space. In 2018, then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe included strengthening capabilities in the space domain, along with electromagnetic and cyber fields, as a key priority in the 'National Defense Program Guidelines,' which outline long-term defense strategies. (일본은 2012년 자민당이 다시 집권한 후 자위대의 활동 영역을 우주로 확대한다는 구상을 지속적으로 추진해왔습니다. 2018년 아베 신조(安倍晋三) 당시 총리는 장기 방위 전략을 다룬 ‘방위계획 대강(大綱)’에 전자파·사이버 분야와 함께 우주 분야의 역량 강화를 중점 추진 과제로 포함시켰습니다.)

At the 2019 U.S.-Japan Security Consultative Committee (2+2) meeting, a joint statement was issued agreeing to cooperate not only in cyberspace but also in space. At the time, the Nikkei newspaper analyzed that "as the hegemonic struggle over space between the U.S. and China intensifies, Japan, as an ally of the U.S., is also being called upon to strengthen its (space force) system." (2019년 미일 외교·국방장관 2+2 회의에서는 사이버 공간은 물론 우주에서도 협력한다는 합의문을 발표했습니다. 당시 니혼게이자이신문은 “미중 간 우주를 둘러싼 패권 다툼이 격렬해지면서 미국과 동맹국인 일본도 (우주군) 체제 강화를 요구받고 있다”고 분석했습니다.)

The space unit of the Japan Air Self-Defense Force, newly established in 2020, is not an independent military branch but is expanding its domain. It primarily conducts missions to monitor the movements of satellites from China, Russia, etc., in cooperation with the U.S. The close relationship between President Trump and former Prime Minister Abe played a significant role in the backdrop of the U.S.-Japan alliance expanding into space. The two leaders upgraded the U.S.-Japan alliance through the Indo-Pacific vision while also initiating full-fledged cooperation in space. (2020년 신설된 일본 항공자위대의 우주 부대는 독립 군종은 아니지만, 그 영역을 확대하고 있습니다. 미국과 협력하에 중국·러시아 등의 인공위성 동향을 감시하는 임무를 주로 수행합니다. 미일동맹이 우주로 확대되는 배경에는 트럼프 대통령과 아베 전 총리의 긴밀한 관계가 큰 역할을 했습니다. 두 정상은 인도·태평양 구상을 매개로 미·일동맹을 업그레이드하면서 우주에서의 협력도 본격화했습니다.)

Japan Collects 4.5g Sample from an Asteroid (소행성에서 4.5g 시료 채취한 일본)

U.S.-Japan space cooperation is built upon Japan's long-accumulated space-related technologies. Japan established a space center on Tanegashima Island, off the southern tip of Kagoshima Prefecture, in 1969 and has focused on space development at the government-wide level. As a result, Japan has acquired the scientific and technological capability to create an artificial crater on the asteroid 'Ryugu,' located about 300 million km from Earth, using its Hayabusa2 probe. (미일 우주 협력에는 일본이 오랫동안 축적해 온 우주 관련 기술이 기반이 됐습니다. 일본은 1969년 가고시마 남단의 다네가시마(種子島)에 우주센터를 만들어 범정부 차원에서 우주 개발에 주력해 왔습니다. 일본은 그 결과 지구에서 약 3억㎞ 떨어진 소행성 ‘류구’에 탐사선 하야부사2를 보내 인공 웅덩이(crater)를 만들 정도의 과학기술력을 갖게 됐습니다.)

Japan was the first country to attempt collecting a sample by creating an artificial crater on an asteroid. (소행성에 인공 웅덩이를 만들어 시료 채취를 시도한 것은 일본이 처음입니다.)

Based on this technological prowess, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) is also pursuing a plan to send a manned lander to the moon by 2030. JAXA aims to send a lander to the lunar surface for exploration about once a year, for a total of around five missions. (일본 우주항공연구개발기구(JAXA)는 이런 기술력을 바탕으로 2030년 달에 유인 착륙기를 보내기 위한 구상도 추진 중입니다. JAXA는 매년 한 차례, 총 5차례 정도 착륙선을 달 표면에 보내 탐사하는 것을 목표로 하고 있습니다.)

I witnessed Japan's interest in space firsthand during my time as a Tokyo correspondent in 2020. On December 6, 2020, soil samples collected from the asteroid 'Ryugu,' located 300 million km from Earth by Japan's unmanned probe Hayabusa2, arrived on Earth. It was six years after the probe departed Earth in 2014. (Ryugu is an asteroid orbiting between Earth and Mars, named by Japan, which discovered it.) (일본의 우주에 대한 관심을 현장에서 목격한 것은 지난 2020년 도쿄 특파원 시절입니다. 2020년 12월 6일 일본 무인 탐사선 하야부사2가 지구에서 3억㎞ 떨어진 소행성 ‘류구’에서 채집한 토양 시료가 지구에 도착했습니다. 탐사선이 2014년 지구를 출발한 지 6년 만이었습니다. (류구는 지구와 화성 사이를 도는 소행성으로 일본이 발견해 붙인 이름입니다.))

According to JAXA, a capsule separated from Hayabusa2 in space, about 220,000 km from Earth, entered the atmosphere at around 3 a.m. on December 6th at a speed of 12 km per second. The capsule, enduring atmospheric heat of about 3,000 degrees Celsius, deployed a parachute and landed in the planned Woomera desert in Australia around 3:00 a.m. JAXA personnel dispatched to Australia used helicopters to search for radio signals emitted by the capsule and successfully recovered it. (JAXA에 따르면 5일 오후 지구에서 약 22만㎞ 떨어진 우주 공간에서 하야부사2에서 분리된 캡슐은 6일 새벽 초속 12㎞로 대기권에 진입했습니다. 약 3000도 대기권 열을 이겨낸 캡슐은 이후 낙하산을 펼쳐 예정했던 호주 우메라 사막에 오전 3시쯤 착륙했습니다. 호주에 파견된 JAXA 요원들은 헬리콥터를 동원, 캡슐에서 발신되는 전파를 찾아가는 방식으로 수색 작전을 벌여 캡슐을 회수했습니다.)

It was so flawless that Japanese media (Nikkei) called it a "perfect success." Then-Prime Minister Yoshihide Suga also expressed his delight on Twitter. (일본 언론이 한 치의 어긋남도 없는 ‘완전완벽(完全完璧)한 성공’(니혼게이자이신문)이라고 평가할 정도로 완벽했습니다. 스가 요시히데(菅義偉) 당시 총리도 트위터를 통해 “매우 기쁘다”고 했습니다.)

Most asteroids are rock fragments formed during the birth of the solar system 4.6 billion years ago. Japan expected the collected material to be used in research to unravel the evolution of the solar system and the mysteries of life. (소행성 대부분은 46억년 전 태양계가 탄생할 당시 발생한 암석 파편들입니다. 일본은 채취한 물질이 태양계 진화 및 생명의 신비를 푸는 연구에 활용될 것으로 기대했습니다.)

The asteroid sample that Hayabusa2 brought back to Earth was initially expected to be only 0.1g, but the actual recovery of 5.4g excited space researchers. Studies revealed that the Ryugu sample contained minerals formed by reaction with water and primordial organic materials preserved in a nearly uncontaminated state. This raised the possibility that asteroids formed in the outer solar system and then carried water to Earth. (하야부사2가 지구로 가져온 소행성 시료는 당초 0.1g만으로 예상했으나, 실제로는 5.4g이 회수되면서 우주 연구자들을 흥분시켰습니다. 연구 결과 류구 시료에는 물과 반응해 생성된 광물과 원시 유기물이 거의 오염되지 않은 상태로 보존돼 있었습니다. 소행성이 태양계 외곽에서 형성된 뒤 물을 품은 채 지구로 이동했을 가능성이 제기됐습니다.)

Furthermore, researchers identified organic molecules that constitute life and nucleobases that make up DNA and RNA in the Ryugu sample, speculating that the building blocks of life may have been delivered to early Earth via asteroids. Japanese researchers evaluate the samples brought back by Hayabusa2 as becoming a 'universal standard sample' for elucidating the formation of the solar system, water, organic matter, and the origin of life. (또 연구진은 류구 시료에서 생명체를 이루는 유기 분자와 DNA·RNA를 구성하는 핵염기 성분을 확인, 생명의 재료가 소행성을 통해 초기 지구에 전달됐을 가능성이 있다고 추측하기도 합니다. 일본 연구진은 하야부사2가 가져온 시료가 태양계 형성과 물, 유기물, 생명의 기원을 규명하는 ‘우주 표준 시료’로 자리 잡고 있다고 평가하고 있습니다.)

Japan Demonstrates Technology to Defend Earth from Comet Impacts (일본, 혜성의 지구 충돌 방어 기술 입증 )

After returning to Earth's orbit after traveling approximately 5.2 billion km and releasing its capsule, Hayabusa2 flew towards another asteroid, where it is scheduled to land in 2031. Continuing its mission, Hayabusa2 on the 5th of this month successfully demonstrated Planetary Defense technology to prevent Earth collisions with asteroids or comets. Until now, the U.S. was the only country possessing this technology, and Japan has now joined it. (하야부사2는 약 52억㎞ 비행 끝에 지구 궤도로 돌아와 캡슐을 분리시킨 후, 2031년 착륙 예정인 다른 소행성을 향해 날아갔습니다. 그러던 중 ‘하야부사2′는 이후에도 운행을 계속하다가 지난 5일 소행성이나 혜성과의 지구 충돌을 막는 플래네터리 디펜스(Planetary Defense·행성 방어) 기술을 실증하는 데 성공했습니다. 이 기술을 보유한 국가는 미국뿐이었는데, 일본이 여기에 합류한 것입니다.)

In this experiment, targeting the asteroid 'Torifune' located about 100 million km from Earth, Hayabusa2 performed a high-speed flyby, passing the asteroid at approximately 18,000 km/h. It captured Torifune with its onboard camera, collected data with its sensors, and autonomously controlled its orbit to approach within 400-600 meters of Torifune's surface. The Nikkei newspaper, citing a JAXA official, reported that this success was as difficult as "accurately hitting a 1-yen coin located in Hokkaido from Okinawa, Japan." This demonstrated that while Japan generally lags behind the 'big three' space powers—the U.S., China, and Russia—in overall space-related technology, it has reached parity with the U.S. in asteroid exploration. (이 실험은 지구에서 약 1억㎞ 떨어진 소행성 ‘토리후네’를 목표로 ‘하야부사2′가 시속 약 1만8000㎞의 초고속으로 소행성을 스쳐 지나가는 비행을 수행했습니다. 탑재된 카메라로 토리후네를 포착, 센서로 데이터를 수집하며 스스로 궤도를 제어해 토리후네 표면 400~600m 지점까지 접근한 겁니다. 니혼게이자이신문은 JAXA 관계자를 인용, “일본 오키나와에서 홋카이도에 있는 1엔짜리 동전을 정확히 맞히는 것만큼 어려운 일”을 성공했다고 밝혔습니다. 이로써 일본은 전반적인 우주 관련 기술은 우주 3강인 미국·중국·러시아에 뒤처져 있지만 소행성 탐사는 미국과 어깨를 나란히 할 정도가 됐음을 입증했습니다.)

Japan Preparing for the Era of Space Management (우주 경영 시대 대비하는 일본 )

Japan's space strategy is a move to prepare for the upcoming era of 'Space Management.' The World Economic Forum and McKinsey project that the global space economy will grow about threefold, from $630 billion in 2023 to $1.8 trillion by 2035. They forecast that satellite communication, positioning and navigation, and Earth observation technologies will combine with almost all terrestrial industries such as logistics, agriculture, and energy, growing faster than the global economic growth rate. (일본의 우주 전략은 앞으로 본격화될 ‘우주 경영(宇宙經營)’ 시대에 대비하려는 움직임입니다. 세계경제포럼과 맥킨지는 세계 우주 경제 규모가 2023년 6300억달러에서 2035년 1조8000억달러로 약 세 배 성장할 것으로 전망했습니다. 위성통신과 위치·항법, 지구 관측 기술이 물류·농업·에너지 등 지상의 거의 모든 산업과 결합, 세계 경제성장률보다 빠르게 성장할 것이라는 전망입니다.)

Just as Spain and Portugal, which secured advanced navigation skills from the 15th to 18th centuries, dominated global management by controlling the oceans, countries possessing lunar and asteroid exploration capabilities, space resource development, satellite networks, and launch vehicle technology are likely to lead the new economic order in the future. Space development is also notable for driving advanced industries like semiconductors, artificial intelligence, robotics, communications, new materials, and energy. (15~18세기 첨단 항해술을 확보한 스페인과 포르투갈 등이 해양을 장악하며 세계 경영을 주도했듯이, 앞으로는 달과 소행성 탐사, 우주 자원 개발, 위성망과 발사체 기술을 보유한 나라가 새로운 경제 질서를 주도할 가능성이 큽니다. 우주 개발이 반도체와 인공지능, 로봇, 통신, 신소재, 에너지 등 첨단 산업을 견인한다는 점에서도 주목됩니다.)

With this awareness, the Japanese government and private companies are joining forces to promote lunar exploration and space industry development. Toyota Motor Corporation and JAXA are jointly developing a manned pressurized rover called the 'Lunar Cruiser,' in which two astronauts can live without spacesuits for up to a month while exploring the lunar surface. Japan plans to provide this vehicle to the U.S. Artemis program in exchange for securing opportunities for Japanese astronauts to operate on the lunar surface. (일본은 이러한 인식 아래 정부와 민간기업이 결합해 달 탐사와 우주산업 육성에 나서고 있습니다. 도요타자동차와 JAXA는 우주비행사 2명이 우주복을 벗은 채 길게는 한 달 동안 생활하며 달 표면을 탐사할 수 있는 유인 가압 로버 ‘루나 크루저’를 공동 개발하고 있습니다. 일본은 이 차량을 미국의 아르테미스 계획에 제공하고 그 대가로 일본인 우주비행사의 달 표면 활동 기회를 확보한다는 구상입니다.)

The Japanese space startup ispace is also challenging the private lunar transportation business, developing its own lunar lander and small exploration rover. ispace's second lunar lander, 'Resilience,' failed to complete its mission in 2025 due to communication loss during its lunar landing attempt. Although a failure, it is considered an achievement that a Japanese private company has accumulated technology to fly through space 1.1 million km from Earth and transport cargo to lunar orbit. Based on these trials, Japan continues to push for entry into the 'lunar economy,' where private companies handle surface transportation, communications, and resource surveys. (일본의 우주 스타트업 아이스페이스도 자체 달 착륙선과 소형 탐사차를 개발하며 민간 달 운송 사업에 도전하고 있습니다. 아이스페이스의 두 번째 달 착륙선 ‘레질리언스’는 2025년 달 착륙 과정에서 통신이 끊겨 임무를 완료하지 못했습니다. 비록 실패했지만, 일본 민간 기업이 지구에서 110만㎞ 떨어진 우주를 비행하고 달 궤도까지 화물을 운반하는 기술을 축적했다는 점은 성과로 평가됩니다. 일본은 이 같은 시행착오를 바탕으로 달 표면 운송과 통신, 자원 조사 등을 민간 기업이 담당하는 ‘달 경제권’ 진입을 계속 추진하고 있습니다.)

South Korea Also Needs a National-Level Long-Term Strategy (한국도 국가 차원의 장기 전략이 필요)

South Korea has also begun to seriously pursue the K-Starlink project and lunar exploration plans. However, it is true that the approach of binding security, industry, and private enterprise into a single national strategy and pursuing it over the long term, as Japan does, is still lacking. (한국도 K-Starlink 구축과 달 탐사 계획을 본격 추진하기 시작했습니다. 그러나 일본처럼 안보와 산업, 민간 기업을 하나의 국가 전략으로 묶어 장기간 추진하는 접근법이 아직 부족한 것이 사실입니다.)

Above all, it seems necessary to nationally recognize space as a strategic asset directly linked to national security that simultaneously expands future industries and economic territory. I hope we will fully prepare for the 'era of space management' by studying Japan's long-term strategy and public-private cooperation model. An era seems to be drawing near where the country that preempts space will lead the future economy and security. (무엇보다 전 국가적으로 우주를 국가 안보와 직결되고, 미래 산업과 경제 영토를 동시에 확장하는 전략 자산으로 인식하는 것이 필요해 보입니다. 일본의 장기 전략과 민관 협력 모델을 참고, ‘우주 경영 시대’에 본격 대비하기를 바랍니다. 우주를 선점하는 나라가 미래 경제와 안보를 주도하는 시대가 성큼 다가와 있는 듯합니다.)

<<>> ()

item.title: Kim Yong-beom: “Delisting Samsung Electronics-SK Hynix Leverage ETFs Is Difficult... Considering Various Options” (김용범 “삼전닉스 레버리지, 상장폐지는 어려워... 다양한 방법 고민”)
item.description:
Kim Yong-beom: “Delisting Samsung Electronics-SK Hynix Leverage ETFs Is Difficult... Considering Various Options” (김용범 “삼전닉스 레버리지, 상장폐지는 어려워... 다양한 방법 고민”)

Kim Yong-beom, head of the policy office at the presidential office, stated on the 19th regarding the controversy over single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix: “Delisting is realistically difficult to consider,” adding, “We need to further explore various ways to minimize market impact.” <<> Appearing on KBS’s “Sunday Diagnosis” that day, Director Kim said, “If we delist a product that investors are already invested in, with a scale exceeding 10 trillion won, it would itself cause a massive shock to the market.” <<> He highlighted the issue of the premium/discount rate—the gap between the market price and the net asset value of ETF products—noting, “There is an aspect where market impact occurs as buying and selling are concentrated in the last 30 minutes before market close to adjust the premium/discount rate.” He added, “It seems the authorities and securities firms need to engage in further dialogue, including whether the premium/discount rate management period must strictly be within 30 minutes, whether the time frame can be expanded, or whether it can be managed through methods other than spot trading.” <<> Regarding recent remarks by Financial Supervisory Service Governor Lee Chan-jin, who said about single-stock leveraged ETFs, “I personally reflect on whether I should have blocked it by lying down,” Director Kim commented, “I later heard him say his intent was that reviews or similar processes should have been stricter,” and added, “It was a decision made through mutual consultation.” <<> On the real estate market, Director Kim said, “I am truly sorry to the people,” and assessed, “Both supply and demand sides are in a very challenging situation.” He stated, “We are trying to secure short-term effective supply volumes by mobilizing them comprehensively, including non-apartment housing, purchase-lease properties, officetel supply, and conversion of commercial land to residential use.” Regarding the plan to use semi-industrial zones in Seoul for housing supply, he said, “It’s not just a Seoul city issue; collaboration with the central government could yield much greater results, so I’ve made an appointment to meet separately with Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon.” <<> On tax reform directions, he said, “At the discussion forum, many opinions were raised that even for single-home owner-occupied properties, very high-priced homes should be viewed differently from mid-priced homes, considering factors like affordability and impact on the housing market, and there is some judgment on that direction.” He added, “The appropriate price level and criteria will be determined after hearing more public opinions and discussions, and will be included in the tax reform proposal to be announced at the end of this month.” Regarding the relationship between property-holding taxes and capital gains taxes, he said, “We are taking it fully into account,” but added, “It’s difficult to uniformly say that raising property-holding taxes must necessarily lower capital gains taxes.” <<> Meanwhile, regarding the criticism that Korea’s promised investment projects in the U.S. as a quid pro quo for tariff reductions are being delayed, Director Kim responded, “That’s not the case. It’s progressing on a proper schedule,” and said, “We are preparing to realize the first U.S. investment project.” When asked about the timing of making the U.S. investments visible, he replied, “It should happen by August or September, shouldn’t it?” <<>> (김용범 청와대 정책실장이 19일 삼성전자·SK하이닉스 단일종목 레버리지 상장지수펀드(ETF) 논란에 대해 “상장 폐지는 사실 생각하기 어렵다”며 “시장 충격을 최소화할 수 있는 다양한 방법을 더 고민해야 한다”고 했다.)

item.title: Yoo Si-min Goes One-on-One with Lee Jae-myung, While the ‘Moon-Jo-Teo-Lae’ Faction Sits on the Sidelines (유시민 나홀로 李와 맞짱, ‘문조털래’는 관망 중)
item.description:
Yoo Si-min Goes One-on-One with Lee Jae-myung, While the ‘Moon-Jo-Teo-Lae’ Faction Sits on the Sidelines (유시민 나홀로 李와 맞짱, ‘문조털래’는 관망 중)

Author Yoo Si-min’s remark that “the Lee Jae-myung administration is bound to fail” has sent a megaton shockwave through the ruling party. It is unprecedented for a figure within the ruling party to declare the government’s inevitable failure just over a year after its inception. Within the pro-Lee faction, there is backlash, with comments like “This is not something to say to a sitting president who has only been in office for a little over a year” and “The curses and slander have crossed the line.” This underscores how provocative Yoo’s remarks are and the immense political shock they carry. <<> Yoo appeared on the YouTube show *Maebul Show* on the 15th and stated, “President Lee Jae-myung is making very wrong judgments in terms of (prosecution reform and managing state affairs), and he is heading down an inevitable path of failure.” He added, “The lack of progress in prosecution reform for over a year is because the president doesn’t want it.” He further remarked, “The president himself should have handled this responsibly, but instead, he’s using a tactic from Machiavelli’s *The Prince*—making subordinates take the heat.” <<> Regarding the Democratic Party’s national convention, Yoo said, “It’s not that (the president) explicitly told Chung Cheong-rae not to run, but he has repeatedly worked to promote former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok.” On the nominations for the June 3 by-elections, he commented, “They need to stop forcing the president’s picks, but there has been too much intervention of that kind. The Democratic Party should not be dominated by the president. If it continues, the party will disintegrate.” <<> Criticizing the pro-Lee faction’s control of the party, Yoo argued, “We expected an expansion, but the president seems to be thinking in terms of reconstruction and redevelopment. That’s highly likely to lead to disastrous results.” Each word was a sharp, direct jab at the president. It’s no wonder that some are evaluating this as Yoo declaring open war against President Lee and the pro-Lee faction. <<> Yoo’s aggressive offensive primarily stems from deep dissatisfaction with the government’s policy direction. The government’s lukewarm stance on abolishing the supplementary investigative powers of the prosecution is seen by some as possibly linked to the dismissal of charges in the president’s own case. This appears to take into account the theory, raised within the party, of a “trade-off between dropping charges and the prosecution’s supplementary investigative powers.” There is also significant accumulated discontent over the government’s pragmatic stance and its appointment of figures from the opposition camp. <<> A more fundamental reason is the struggle for party leadership. Yoo criticized the president for interfering in the national convention, alleging blatant intervention to make former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok, a pro-Lee figure, the party leader. Yoo is close to former leader Chung Cheong-rae. The sentiment is that he cannot stand idly by while Kim Min-seok, backed by the president’s will, becomes the party leader. <<> The pro-Roh and pro-Moon factions within the party consider themselves the original owners of the Democratic Party. Yoo positions himself as their spokesperson. From their perspective, it’s unacceptable that the “unpedigreed” pro-Lee faction has seized the party’s helm and even controls nomination rights for the next general election. The underlying sentiment is a determination not to repeat the “massacre” of pro-Moon figures through “pro-Lee purge” nominations in the last general election. <<> However, the pro-Lee faction has bristled, saying Yoo’s words have gone too far. Criticism is pouring in, calling it “poisonous words that create enemies,” “curses and slander rooted in an elitist mindset,” and “a political provocation to boost his own presence.” Some pro-Lee figures have attacked Yoo, saying, “He’s someone who has only ever shot from outside the party during Democratic Party administrations.” <<> The ruling party is keeping a close watch on whether Yoo’s provocation is a solo act or a coordinated move made with the tacit agreement of the pro-Roh, pro-Moon, and pro-Chung factions. While it appears on the surface to be a solo play, there is speculation that the so-called “Moon-Jo-Teo-Lae-Yoo” inner circle—key figures in the pro-Roh and pro-Moon camp—may have exerted influence behind the scenes. <<> So far, no organized movement from the pro-Roh and pro-Moon factions has surfaced. Former President Moon Jae-in is said not to have been involved in this matter. Unsurprisingly, he has made no statement. YouTuber Kim Eo-jun, who is close to Yoo, also did not directly involve himself this time. Yoo made these remarks on *Maebul Show* instead of Kim Eo-jun’s YouTube channel, where he is a regular guest. Some interpret this as Kim Eo-jun pursuing a dual strategy between Chung Cheong-rae and Kim Min-seok. <<> Former leader of the Rebuilding Korea Party, Cho Kuk, saw his influence significantly wane after the June 3 by-election defeat. He has also refrained from offering any separate opinion on this matter. Former leader Chung Cheong-rae responded with “No comment” regarding Yoo’s remarks, appearing to be cautious with his words. <<> It’s no exaggeration to say that the entire “Moon-Jo-Teo-Lae” network, except for Yoo, is watching from the sidelines. This makes it look like Yoo is going head-to-head with the president all by himself. Given that Yoo has a considerable unfavorable image both inside and outside the party, and faces strong aversion from the pro-Lee faction, the prospect of success if he wages a solo war seems slim. <<> However, regarding the supplementary investigative powers issue, pro-Chung members and hardline party supporters continue to attack pro-Lee lawmakers. It is still too early to guarantee that former PM Kim Min-seok holds a clear advantage in the convention sentiment. Among the hardline party members who will actually vote and the pro-Roh/pro-Moon support base, support for former leader Chung Cheong-rae remains substantial. If the “Moon-Jo-Teo-Lae” faction joins the fray and backs Yoo, the outcome of the “Lee vs. Yoo war” could become unpredictable. <<> The direct reason Yoo stirred up a storm in the ruling party with his extreme remarks is his dissatisfaction with the policy direction of the Lee Jae-myung government. It served as a kind of warning shot. The abolition of the supplementary investigative powers is a core demand of the pro-Roh, pro-Moon, and hardline supporters, and is tied to the party’s identity. Yoo believes that President Lee is behind attempts within the pro-Lee faction to retain these powers. <<> Yoo suspects that President Lee is trying to roll back the supplementary investigative powers to resolve his primary concern—his legal risks, specifically seeking the dismissal of charges in various cases. Several months ago, some panelists on Kim Eo-jun’s YouTube channel also raised the theory of a trade-off between the prosecution’s supplementary investigative powers and the dropping of charges. <<> Dissatisfaction with the government’s pragmatic policies and personnel appointments, which are perceived as deviating from progressive lines, likely also played a role. The pro-Roh and pro-Moon faction, being the most progressive within the Democratic Party, has experienced ongoing policy conflicts with the pro-Lee faction, which emphasizes pragmatism. Resentment has also built up over President Lee’s successive appointments of figures from the People Power Party or conservative backgrounds. <<> The most crucial reason is the unwillingness to hand over the party’s hegemony to the pro-Lee faction led by the “New Lee Jae-myung.” A few months ago, Yoo, through his “ABC theory,” directly targeted the pro-Lee faction, calling them “Group B that pursues only interests, not the value-centric Group A.” His argument is that the Democratic Party’s roots lie with the pro-Roh and pro-Moon factions, so why should the “unpedigreed” pro-Lee faction control the party? The stated issue may be supplementary investigative powers, but the essence is a struggle for party leadership. Yoo’s provocation is widely interpreted as an attempt to shake up the landscape before the national convention. <<> Pro-Lee lawmakers are seething over Yoo’s statement that the president will fail, calling it “slander that has crossed a significant line.” They believe Yoo made a deliberate provocation to boost his own presence. Yoo has long acted as a self-appointed spokesperson for the pro-Roh and pro-Moon factions, and is known to believe he played a major role in getting President Lee elected. Pro-Lee lawmakers argue that Yoo has exhibited this behavior in the past to expand his political influence and provoke opponents. <<> Lawmaker Park Jie-won said, “Yoo harassed (Kim Dae-jung) throughout the five years of his government and even proclaimed the ‘D-J will fail’ theory.” A pro-Lee figure criticized, “Yoo has always been an internal saboteur operating from outside the Democratic Party,” and “Attacking allies is his specialty, more than attacking the opposition.” <<> Whether Yoo’s provocative remarks are a solo act or reflect the collective will of the pro-Roh and pro-Moon factions is also crucial. On the surface, it appears to be a solo play. This is because pro-Roh and pro-Moon figures who might jointly respond with Yoo are not readily visible. However, the possibility that the sentiments of the pro-Moon camp are being communicated tacitly cannot be ruled out. <<> This brings the focus to the so-called “Moon-Jo-Teo-Lae” sentiment. Firstly, former President Moon Jae-in reportedly neither involved himself in this matter nor discussed it with Yoo. In a recent meeting with President Lee, Moon emphasized “party unity.” While his inner thoughts might have differed, his outward stance was one of cooperation and resolving conflicts together. <<> Kim Eo-jun, who usually comments on every political issue, has not joined the fray regarding Yoo’s remarks. Yoo, a frequent guest on Kim’s YouTube channel, chose to make his controversial statement on *Maebul Show* this time. This has led to speculation that Yoo went to a different show because Kim Eo-jun didn’t set the stage for him. <<> Kim Eo-jun recently appeared to side with former PM Kim Min-seok by playing a video of him climbing over the National Assembly fence on the day martial law was declared. This has prompted assessments that Kim Eo-jun might be playing both sides between former leader Chung and former PM Kim. However, on the 16th, Kim strongly argued for the abolition of the supplementary investigative powers. At least on this issue, he echoes Yoo’s voice. <<> When asked for his opinion on Yoo’s remarks, former leader Chung Cheong-rae was tight-lipped, saying “No comment.” He appears to be playing it safe, wary of potential backlash at the convention if he openly sides with Yoo. However, regarding the supplementary investigative powers, he stated, “I will see this through to the end,” indicating he shares Yoo’s view. <<> Former leader Cho Kuk has also refrained from speaking out on this matter. Not long ago, he faced backlash for labeling a K-pop idol group’s speech as reminiscent of “Ilbe slang.” Cho is known to have maintained behind-the-scenes communication with President Lee. This may make it difficult for him to readily join Yoo’s criticism of the president. Nevertheless, the support base of the Rebuilding Korea Party is reportedly in strong agreement with Yoo’s remarks. <<> The presidential office has not directly responded to Yoo’s remarks. While clearly displeased, they have stated, “We have no intention of responding to a specific individual’s remarks.” Directly confronting Yoo might create a narrative of a “one-on-one fight” between President Lee and Yoo. It could escalate the convention from a contest between former PM Kim Min-seok and former leader Chung Cheong-rae into a struggle between the president and Chung. This is seen as an attempt to minimize the impact on the convention by avoiding political controversy. <<> Former PM Kim Min-seok is also maintaining a reserved stance. Former leader Song Young-gil tempered his tone, saying, “I understand his loyalty, but expressions of curses or slander are not appropriate.” Instead, pro-Lee lawmakers are waging a proxy war. The presidential office, former PM Kim, and former leader Song have indicated no change in their stance on abolishing supplementary investigative powers. They appear to be moving cautiously to prevent the supplementary investigative powers issue from becoming a variable in the convention. <<> How will the war for hegemony within the ruling party, sparked by Yoo, unfold? Will Yoo succeed in this war? The key barometer is the fate of the supplementary investigative powers. Following revelations of poor police investigation and collusion suspicions in the case of Jang Yoon-gi, opposition from women’s groups, the legal community, and even within the ruling party is growing. Polls show opposition exceeding 60%, significantly diminishing the momentum for abolishing the powers. <<> However, since Yoo’s remarks, hardline party supporters have reportedly been bombarding lawmakers who proposed legislation to retain the supplementary investigative powers with text messages. This has made the presidential office and pro-Lee party leadership candidates hesitant to openly advocate for retaining them. Consequently, the growing sentiment within the ruling party to postpone the abolition may stall. <<> Yoo’s remarks could also become a variable in the party leadership race. After the local elections, a trend of “Chung Cheong-rae weakening, Kim Min-seok strengthening” was evident. Now, there is speculation that Yoo’s remarks could serve as a rallying point for the pro-Roh, pro-Moon, and pro-Chung factions. Some signs indicate that hardline Honam party members and the Rebuilding Korea Party support base are coalescing behind Chung Cheong-rae. <<> However, there is considerable antipathy towards Yoo within the ruling party. He is widely criticized for only boosting his own presence by engaging in internal strife at every opportunity. An “anti-Yoo Si-min” or “anti-Chung Cheong-rae” backlash from ordinary party members or supporters is possible. Furthermore, public opinion favoring the retention of supplementary investigative powers is growing. Ultimately, whether Yoo’s war succeeds will be determined at the Democratic Party’s national convention scheduled for the 17th of next month. (유시민 작가의 ‘이재명 정부 필패’ 발언이 여권에 메가톤급 파문을 일으키고 있습니다. 정권 출범 1년여 만에 여권 인사가 정부 필패론을 꺼낸 건 전례가 없는 일입니다. 친명 내부에선 “취임 1년여밖에 안 된 현직 대통령에게 할 말이 아니다” “저주와 악담이 도를 넘었다”고 반발하고 있습니다. 그만큼 유씨의 발언이 도발적이고 정치적 충격파가 크다는 뜻입니다.)

item.title: Spouse of the Late Lee Hae-chan Becomes Chairman of Chung Cheong-rae’s Support Committee… “I Will Carry on the Legacy of the Former Party Leader” (정청래 후원회장에 故 이해찬 배우자… “선배 당대표 뜻 잇겠다”)
item.description:
Chung Cheong-rae, a former lawmaker running in the Democratic Party of Korea’s August 17 party convention leadership election, announced on the 19th that Kim Jeong-ok, the spouse of the late former Prime Minister Lee Hae-chan, has agreed to serve as the chair of his support committee. (더불어민주당 8·17 전당대회 당대표 선거에 출마한 정청래 전 대표는 19일 고(故) 이해찬 전 국무총리의 배우자인 김정옥 여사가 후원회장을 맡기로 했다고 밝혔다.)

In a Facebook post that day, Chung revealed his recent meeting with Madam Kim, stating, “The moment I heard that Madam Kim was willing to serve as the chair of my support committee, I felt a heavy sense of responsibility weighing on my shoulders.” (정 전 대표는 이날 페이스북에서 최근 김 여사와 만났다는 사실을 알리며 “김 여사께서 제 후원회장을 기꺼이 맡아주시겠다는 말씀을 듣는 순간 정말 무거운 책임감에 어깨가 무거웠다”고 했다.)

Chung said, “I was struck by the weight of it, as if another living Prime Minister Lee Hae-chan were speaking, and the responsibility to not tarnish the honor of Prime Minister Lee Hae-chan swept over me.” He added, “I told Madam, ‘Making the Democratic Party truly democratic! A strong reformist party leader’ is my slogan, and I pledged to become exactly that kind of party leader.” (정 전 대표는 “살아있는 또 한 분의 이해찬 총리님께서 말씀하시는 듯한 무게감, 이해찬 총리님의 명예에 누가 되지 않아야 한다는 책임감이 엄습했다”며 “사모님께 ‘민주당을 민주당답게! 강력한 개혁당대표’가 제 슬로건이고 또 꼭 그런 당대표가 되겠다고 말씀드렸다”고 전했다.)

He continued, “I told her that internally, I aim for ‘four-way integration,’ externally for unity and solidarity, and that the Democratic Party’s identity lies in reform upon reform, and I vowed to see prosecutorial reform through to the end.” He added, “Madam emphasized the Democratic Party’s identity and legitimacy over and over, saying, ‘Please make sure to do that.’” (그는 “당 안으로 ‘4통 통합’, 당 밖으로 통합과 연대, 그리고 민주당의 정체성은 개혁하고 또 개혁이고, 검찰개혁을 꼭 완수하겠다고 말씀드렸다”며 “사모님께서는 ‘꼭 그렇게 해달라’며 민주당 정체성과 정통성을 내내 강조하셨다”고 했다.)

Chung then stated, “With the spirit of Lee Hae-chan, I will complete prosecutorial reform and make the Democratic Party a more reform-oriented party. As a junior party leader, I will carry on the path of my senior party leader, upholding his will, and with the spirit of Lee Hae-chan, I will transform the Democratic Party into a democratic, people’s party that wins through reform.” (정 전 대표는 그러면서 “이해찬 정신으로 검찰 개혁을 완수하고 민주당을 더 개혁적인 정당으로 만들겠다”며 “선배 당대표의 길을 후배 당대표로서 그 뜻을 이어가면서 이해찬 정신으로 민주당을 민주적 국민 정당, 개혁해서 승리하는 정당으로 만들겠다”고 했다.)

item.title: President Lee: "On raising the party convention deposit, young candidates are struggling; it should be reversed... This is not interference in party affairs" (李대통령, 與 전대 기탁금 인상에 “청년 후보들 힘들어해, 되돌려야...당무개입 아니다”)
item.description:
President Lee Jae-myung said on the 19th regarding the election deposits that candidates running in the Democratic Party of Korea's national convention must pay: "In this party leadership election, the deposit has been significantly raised, and especially for young candidates, it has increased several times, causing them hardship—I find this regrettable." He added, "The party's finances are not in difficulty, and considering the struggles of young people and the need for policy consideration, if possible, I suggest considering restoring the deposit to its previous level." <<> In a post on X (formerly Twitter) that day, President Lee stated: "Sitting lawmakers may have less burden due to their salaries and political funds, but for those outside the National Assembly, especially young people, the burden will be heavy." He further said, "Some might point out this as interference in party affairs, but under current laws and party regulations, the president, as a party member, is allowed to express opinions on the affairs of his affiliated party, so I hope there is no misunderstanding." <<> Earlier, on the 14th, the Democratic Party announced through candidate registration notices that the preliminary election deposit for party leader and supreme council member candidates would be 20 million won. In last year's national convention, the deposit was 15 million won for party leader candidates and 5 million won for supreme council member candidates. <<> In his post that day, President Lee said: "It is sad that people cannot run for office because of money, but it also increases the temptation for corruption. As a senior who overcame the pain of being penniless in youth and broke through barriers of privilege through countless challenges, I want to at least promote the donation accounts for young candidates." <<> President Lee's post that day sparked interpretations within the ruling party that it was a show of support for Jeong Min-cheol, the deputy policy committee chair who registered as a supreme council member candidate. Deputy Jeong had disclosed his personal account to raise funds for the 20 million won deposit and collected donations, but when it was pointed out that this might violate the Political Funds Act, he stated that he had not properly reviewed the legal aspects and would return the funds. Deputy Jeong also expressed on YouTube that for non-incumbent politicians, especially young ones, raising the deposit is not easy. Recently, Deputy Jeong has shown support for President Lee by criticizing figures like Yoo Si-min, who have taken a critical stance toward President Lee. <<> On online bulletin boards mainly used by Democratic Party supporters, responses such as "The president has openly sent a message to rescue the pro-Lee candidate Jeong Min-cheol" have appeared. This comes amid competition between pro-Lee Jae-myung and pro-Jung Chung-rae candidates in the upcoming party leadership and supreme council member elections, with President Lee reportedly issuing a message to aid the pro-Lee Jae-myung candidate. (이재명 대통령은 19일 더불어민주당 전당대회에 출마하는 후보들이 내야 하는 선거 기탁금에 대해 “이번 당 지도부 선거에서 기탁금이 대폭 상향되고 특히 청년 후보의 기탁금은 몇 배로 늘어나 청년 후보들이 힘들어한다니 아쉽다”며 “당의 재정이 어려운 것도 아니고 청년들의 어려움과 정책적 배려의 필요성도 있으니 가능하다면 기탁금을 종전 수준으로 되돌리는 걸 고려해 보시면 어떨까 한다”고 했다.)

item.title: Yoo Si-min’s ‘Lee Will Definitely Lose’ Controversy… Pro-Moon Yoon Geon-young: “Should Be Seen as a Preventive Shot” (유시민 ‘李 필패론’ 논란에… 친문 윤건영 “예방주사로 봐야”)
item.description:
Yoon Geon-young, a lawmaker from the Democratic Party of Korea known as a close aide to former President Moon Jae-in, commented on author Yoo Si-min’s claim that President Lee Jae-myung might interfere in the party leadership primary, saying, “I wonder if it really goes that far,” but added, “Those close to the President consistently talk about former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok.” <<> Lawmaker Yoon stated, “I’ve even heard they emotionally dislike lawmaker Jeong Cheong-rae,” and added, “This inevitably raises suspicion among many party members.” While he finds it hard to believe Yoo’s claim that President Lee is pushing former Prime Minister Kim as the next party leader, his remarks suggest that the behavior of pro-Lee figures could still warrant such doubts. <<> On the 19th, Lawmaker Yoon posted an article titled “Looking at Yoo Si-min Correctly” on Facebook, expressing his stance on the controversy surrounding Yoo’s recent comments. <<> First, he noted, “The whole town is buzzing about author Yoo Si-min’s story,” adding, “Reactions range from very critical to those who understand his earnestness.” <<> He then said, “I found it a bit uncomfortable to listen to,” and “Regardless of whether the content is right or wrong, I wondered if it had to be said this way,” expressing regret over Yoo’s method of raising the issue and the level of his expressions. <<> Lawmaker Yoon remarked, “The point made by Maebul Show host Choi Wook resonated with me,” and “I felt it was regrettable that there wasn’t a softer approach, or a way to discuss it while uniting the faction.” <<> At the same time, he said, “It was like the Yoo Si-min I know,” adding, “When he’s on our side, it’s exhilarating, but when he’s the opponent, it’s painfully piercing to the core. So it might be uncomfortable.” <<> Lawmaker Yoon emphasized that the focus should be on the content of Yoo’s criticism rather than his delivery style. <<> He said, “Some people get angry, claiming author Yoo pointed at the moon and criticized the finger, or that he clenched his fist,” and added, “It would be better to look at the moon he’s pointing at, not his finger.” <<> However, he stated that he finds it difficult to agree with Yoo’s claim about the possible failure of a “structural majority.” <<> Lawmaker Yoon said, “There are logical contradictions in his argument that I can’t easily accept,” and noted, “Especially his diagnosis of the structural majority.” <<> He continued, “In my view, what President Lee referred to as a structural majority is probably about correcting a tilted playing field,” adding, “It seems like a will to flatten the playing field of our society, which has been dominated by conservatives since liberation.” <<> He assessed, “An artificial reorganization of the political landscape is neither possible nor has the momentum right now,” and “Yet author Yoo concluded by presenting the possibility of failure for a structural majority. It feels somewhat logically stretched, unlike him.” <<> He drew a line regarding criticism of Yoo’s attitude and metaphors. Lawmaker Yoon argued, “Author Yoo is a commentator, not a player on the field,” and “I don’t think we should demand the same strict attitude and metaphors required of a player.” <<> Lawmaker Yoon then mentioned specific issues Yoo raised, such as prosecutorial reform and the party leadership primary. <<> Regarding prosecutorial reform, he said, “Author Yoo said the priority is for the President to provide a frank explanation and seek public understanding,” and “I don’t doubt the President’s will to separate investigation and prosecution.” <<> He added, “After all, President Lee is someone who has suffered damage from political prosecutors more than anyone.” <<> Nevertheless, he expressed doubts about the remarks of some who claim to be close to the President. Lawmaker Yoon stated, “Lately, seeing the words and actions of some so-called self-proclaimed presidential aides raises suspicion,” and “Even now, they are demanding supplementary investigative powers,” adding, “That’s how Machiavelli’s The Prince comes into play.” <<> Regarding the party leadership primary, he interpreted that Yoo was arguing that President Lee is effectively supporting former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok. <<> Lawmaker Yoon said, “Author Yoo seems to think the President is unnecessarily interfering in the party,” and “The prime example he gave is supporting former Prime Minister Kim in the party leadership primary.” <<> He then added, “I wonder if it really goes that far,” but noted, “Those close to the President consistently talk about former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok.” <<> He further stated, “I’ve even heard they emotionally dislike lawmaker Jeong Cheong-rae,” and “This inevitably raises suspicion among many party members.” <<> Lawmaker Yoon added that he does not support either former Prime Minister Kim or lawmaker Jeong. <<> He also mentioned that author Yoo had cited the so-called “Myung-pick” controversy as an example, saying, “This is why author Yoo Si-min’s claims are concerning.” <<> He expressed worry, “If what he claims is true or close to the truth, it’s a really serious problem,” adding, “Before even talking about a structural majority, our internal cohesion could crack and collapse.” <<> Lawmaker Yoon argued that Yoo’s claims should be seen as a kind of well-intentioned warning to the party and government. He said, “I wonder if we could see author Yoo Si-min’s statements as a preventive shot for everyone,” adding, “It may not be the time for vaccination, but getting it in advance probably won’t hurt.” <<> He continued, “I hope we can listen and communicate over a glass of makgeolli,” and “I’ve seen many cases where such issues pile up, leading to relationships where people can’t even share a meal. I hope from now on, we can openly share each other’s concerns.” <<> Lawmaker Yoon concluded his post by expressing hope that Yoo’s concerns would not come true. He said, “Author Yoo said he hopes to fail. I feel the same,” and “I sincerely hope his prediction turns out to be completely wrong.” <<> He added, “The Lee Jae-myung administration must succeed,” and “The Moon Jae-in administration came from Park Geun-hye’s impeachment, and the Lee Jae-myung administration from Yoon Seok-yeol’s impeachment. If the Lee Jae-myung administration fails, we won’t even be able to look the people in the eye.” <<> Lawmaker Yoon’s latest stance comes amid growing controversy within the ruling party over Yoo’s so-called “Lee Jae-myung will definitely lose” theory. In political circles, there have been interpretations that Yoo’s comments effectively signal his entry into the Democratic Party’s convention, rallying pro-Roh and pro-Moon factions, and siding with former lawmaker Jeong Cheong-rae against the pro-Lee camp. In this context, with Yoon, a close confidant of former President Moon, distancing himself from Yoo’s expression but insisting that much of his criticism should be heeded, there is a view that he has partially aligned with Yoo’s assessment of the ruling bloc. <<> (문재인 전 대통령의 최측근으로 알려진 윤건영 더불어민주당 의원이 이재명 대통령의 당대표 경선 개입 가능성을 거론한 유시민 작가의 주장에 대해 “설마 그렇게까지일까 싶다”면서도 “대통령과 가까운 이들이 한결같이 김민석 전 총리 이야기를 한다”고 했다.)

]]>
